capabilities_done: The rule of place_markers (R54 F-R54-6) is one helper, sentinels::line_holding; place_markers, footnotes::locate and the new toc::line_of all use it, no second copy
A footnote, endnote or sidenote reference on a glyph-less byte at a line break (host with inline text; footnotes also with resolved stored text) keeps its line instead of reading as overset

A TOC source paragraph opening with a glyph-less marker takes the page and baseline of its first line, in generate_toc and generate_table_of_contents; on a hidden layer it counts as hidden, not overset
Index marks in the gap take the page of their line (generate_index, generate_index_contract), and hidden-layer marks count as hidden
A page range ending on a paragraph terminator ends on that paragraph's page, not the story's last placed page (index_contract scope_end; before: 'x, 1-2', now 'x, 1')
A running-text paragraph match finds a paragraph opening with a glyph-less marker on its own page
A cross-reference destination (text anchor or paragraph start) in the gap resolves its page instead of Unplaced

verdicts.claim_scope: V4-06 sweep of F-R54-6. The validator re-ran the lane's regex at ce644577: 11 matches in 8 files, exactly the lane's list: 3 fixed (sentinels.rs:603, footnotes.rs:244, toc.rs:202), 8 not applicable. Not-applicable claims tested: anchors.rs:270 is the only line-extent lookup among the 8, and its premise holds through real Type: U+FFFC is shaped or refused MissingGlyph, never glyph-less (PROBE-R55-TYPE-1 t9, both providers; Inter has no U+FFFC glyph); footnotes.rs:262, anchors.rs:122, story_tables.rs:120, styles.rs:238, table.rs:282, threaded_reflow.rs:564, :665 read: each matches a paragraph by exact start or a style span, none maps a byte to a line. A wider search of .source.start/.end, cluster bounds and frames/lines scans over layout and interop-layout found no other byte-to-line lookup. One copy of the rule: the only BreakKind::Mandatory gap rule is sentinels.rs:627 inside line_holding; callers sentinels.rs:658, footnotes.rs:270, toc.rs:216; toc_contract, index, index_contract, running and xref go through toc::line_of. Behaviour a (range end on a terminator): correct, PROBE-R55-LOOKUPS-1 l2 and the base run; behaviour b (sentinel in TOC text): real, F-R55-5. Stored-content note hosts stay unplaced with typed outcomes (endnote position None, sidenote in overset; l3); no MT claimed, which is right. Marker placement also checked per byte on one fixture (l4) and through native Type (n5, n6, n7a), which the lane did not run.

declared_readings: A byte in no line span follows line_holding: inside the paragraph's gap by the F-R54-6 break rule; before the paragraph's first glyph its first line; after its last line, terminator included, its last line. A byte inside a line span keeps its old answer. InDesign placement UNVERIFIED (D5)

The toc.rs, toc_contract, index, running and xref path takes the paragraph from story.paragraphs and its lines by position (source start inside the paragraph), because hand-built placements carry paragraph 0 on every line; footnotes uses Line.paragraph, which indexes the paragraphs it reflowed
observations_out_of_scope: Read from code, not changed: TOC entry text and running-text matches keep marker sentinels (toc.rs clean_keeping removes only trailing breaks, U+2028 and tabs), so a heading opening with an index marker now writes U+FDD7 into the generated TOC story. Before this lane such a heading was left out of the TOC. Tests assert page, not this text. Needs its own lane decision
spec_proposals: STU-TYP-207 / STU-LAY-046 / STU-LAY-047: state the line of a glyph-less byte at a line boundary (carried from SMB-R54-FOLLOWUPS-1, now for references, marks and destinations too)
notes.behaviour_change: Index page ranges that end on a paragraph terminator (ToNextStyleChange, ToNextUseOfStyle, ForNextParagraphs) can now end earlier: on real shaping the terminator has no glyph, so they used to fall back to the story's last placed page. Existing id_index_contract tests stayed green because their hand-built lines include the terminator
